stem:
Meena ties a 2 kg bag of rice to a spring balance in her kitchen in Kochi. She knows that the Earth pulls the bag downwards. Her brother says the reading should be written in kilograms, but Meena says weight is a force.
What is the weight of the bag, and in which unit should it be measured?

options.text: The weight is the Earth's pull on the bag and it is measured in newtons.
The weight is the Earth's pull on the bag and it is measured in kilograms.
The weight is the amount of matter in the bag and it is measured in newtons.
The weight is the amount of matter in the bag and it is measured in kilograms.

teacher.key_rationale: Weight is the gravitational pull of the Earth on an object and, being a force, is measured in newtons. Kilograms measure mass (the amount of matter), so only option A correctly pairs the definition with the unit. Option B is the trap for students who correctly identify weight as the Earth's pull but slip back to kilograms as the unit.
